The '''Squeeze theorem''' states:

Let $(a_n)$, $(b_n)$, $(c_n)$ be three [[number sequence]]s.

If

$$
\exists n_1: \forall n>n_1,\,  a_n \leq b_n \leq c_n,
$$

'''and'''

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = \ell = \lim_{n \to \infty} c_n,
$$

then 

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} b_n = \ell
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2449}}</ref>

== Application ==

The convergence of [[number sequence]]s of complexity can be tested via two simpler number sequences that bound it above and below.

{{Hidden example}}

'''Q''': If $b_n=\frac{\sin(n)}{n}$, does $(b_n)$ converge?

'''Solution''':

Let $a_n=\frac{-1}{n}$, $c_n=\frac{1}{n}$,

then

$$
\forall n: a_n \le b_n \le c_n
$$

Since

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n=0=\lim_{n \to \infty} c_n
$$

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} b_n=0 \iff b_n \text{ converges}
$$

{{End hidden}}
